question: Neha, a Chartered Accountant, is CFO of Orbitline Systems Ltd, a fictional unlisted software company raising funds from investors next month. On 30 March, the managing director asks her to record revenue for a large contract that the customer is expected to sign only in April, saying the investors must see higher sales. Discuss the ethical and reporting issues and how Neha should respond.
sources: ICAI Code of Ethics - fundamental principles and the conceptual framework of threats and safeguards
Ind AS 115 Revenue from Contracts with Customers - identifying the contract

points.label: Reporting position
points.description: With no signed or otherwise approved contract at year-end, the Ind AS 115 conditions for a contract are not met, so no revenue can be recognised in March; doing so would misstate the financial statements.
points.basis: Ind AS 115, criteria for identifying a contract with a customer

points.label: Fundamental principles at risk
points.description: Integrity, objectivity and professional behaviour would be breached by knowingly being associated with misleading information.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics: fundamental principles

points.label: Threats
points.description: Intimidation threat from the managing director's pressure and self-interest threat (job security, possible bonus linked to fundraising).
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics: conceptual framework of threats

points.label: Response
points.description: Explain the correct treatment to the managing director, refuse to record the revenue, document the discussion, and escalate to the board or audit committee if pressure continues; consider legal advice and, as a last resort, resignation.
points.basis: ICAI Code of Ethics: resolving ethical conflicts and pressure to breach the fundamental principles

points.label: Wider consequences
points.description: Misleading investors could expose the company and directors to liability for misstatement in fundraising and harm the company's credibility; the auditor would also need to be informed of the facts.
points.basis: Companies Act, 2013: responsibility of directors for financial statements; general law on misrepresentation
